name: Nasdaq-100

fundingForecast.displaySign: positive is earned by a perp long; negative is paid by a perp long

peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: SP500 29.3% with 3/3 replicate support; NVDA 14.7% with 3/3 replicate support; AAPL 13.7% with 3/3 replicate support; MSFT 12.7% with 3/3 replicate support; AMZN 9.7% with 3/3 replicate support; GOOGL 8.3% with 3/3 replicate support; META 6.3% with 3/3 replicate support; TSLA 5.3% with 3/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: S&P 500
peers.reason: The S&P 500 shares the dominant US equity systematic component with the Nasdaq-100 and overlaps heavily in its top constituents, so it is the closest broad-index return comparator; it also offers the deepest peer liquidity at 89.359 USD millions in 24-hour perp turnover.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: A direct large constituent whose AI semiconductor exposure is a central Nasdaq-100 return driver.

peers.name: Apple
peers.reason: Apple is a top-weighted Nasdaq-100 constituent, so its returns are literally part of the target's returns; it is a direct substitute exposure with 7.075 USD millions of 24-hour perp liquidity.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: A direct large constituent with software, cloud, and AI exposure that closely matches the index’s growth profile.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: Amazon is a large Nasdaq-100 constituent combining consumer platform and cloud exposure, two of the index's main return engines, so it ranks above any remote factor analogy.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: Alphabet is a core Nasdaq-100 heavyweight in digital advertising and cloud, so its return is a direct constituent contribution to the target rather than a sector analogy.

peers.name: Meta Platforms
peers.reason: Meta Platforms is a major Nasdaq-100 constituent in digital advertising and AI investment, contributing directly to the index's return through its large weighting.

peers.name: Tesla
peers.reason: Tesla is a significant Nasdaq-100 constituent whose volatile single-name swings are a direct mechanical input to the index's return, rounding out the mega-cap growth exposure.

primary_index_hedge.name: S&P 500
primary_index_hedge.reason: S&P 500 is the cleanest non-target systematic hedge for Nasdaq-100 because it captures the dominant US large-cap equity beta and much of the same mega-cap technology exposure, with 24-hour perp liquidity of 89.359 USD millions.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

underlierSelection.method: highest summed live contract volume; open interest and contract count break ties

model.name: ATM-straddle-implied lognormal distribution
model.description: Each target uses the nearest paired liquid ATM call and put. Their combined ask implies the expiration distribution shown on the chart.
model.measure: option-implied, not a historical or physical forecast
